findings.summary: NEW SURVIVING MUTATION, reachable rather than equivalent: nothing pins that the argument must be on an ADDED line as opposed to a REMOVED one. Mutating the awk selector in scripts/check-reviewed.sh:142 from '/^\+/ && !/^\+\+\+/' to '/^[-+]/ && !/^[-+][-+][-+]/' leaves 15/15 GREEN. Measured in an isolated copy of the harness, not inferred. Under the mutant, substr($0,2) of a deletion line yields the bare key, f[1]==k, rest is non-space, so a STAGED DELETION of a rounds:<task> line argues the cap. Two tests cover neighbouring arms (aROUNDSLineAppearingOnlyAsDIFFCONTEXT uniquely kills the all-diff-lines loosening; aROUNDSLineALREADYCOMMITTED covers the untouched-file case) and neither reaches the deletion arm, because no fixture ever stages a removal from baselines/review.txt.
findings.failure_scenario: An argued commit for task X lands, leaving 'rounds:X  <reason>' committed in baselines/review.txt. A later commit for the SAME task X tidies the file and deletes that now-stale line. With the added-line selector loosened by one character, the deletion itself waives the cap for round 3+ of X -- the escape re-arms on the act of cleaning it up, and the gate prints 'ARGUED as rounds:X'. This is the same direction of failure M4.31 records for a MOVED line (delete+add), one arm further out: M4.31's prescribed primitive (present in `git show :baselines/review.txt`, absent from `git show HEAD:...`) kills it structurally, but M4.31's row names only the moved-line and re-argue cases, so an implementer following that row would not necessarily add a test for the deletion arm. NOT filed as major because it sits inside the added-line primitive M4.31 explicitly split off at round 5, and because production behaviour today is correct -- only the test coverage of it is missing.

notes: Staged hash verified as 8da566e2eb03 before and after all work. Nothing in the working tree was edited: all mutation was done against an isolated copy under a private scratch dir (gradle/, gradlew, buildSrc/, scripts/, settings.gradle.kts, .gitignore, baselines/), and `git status --porcelain` for the staged paths is unchanged.
BASELINE: 15/15 green against the unmutated staged gate, confirmed twice (before and after the sweep) from TEST-binjava.ReviewRoundCapTest.xml: tests=15 failures=0 errors=0 skipped=0.

(1) T6 IS CLOSED, ON ALL THREE ARMS. Pathspec widened to 'baselines/' -> FAILS aFILENAMEThatMerelyMATCHESTheGuardAsAPatternDoesNOTLiftTheCap. Pathspec widened to 'baselines/review*' -> FAILS the same test. And the strengthening did NOT trade one arm for another: the ORIGINAL BRE-basename defect, reproduced as a pathspec in which the dot is a wildcard ('baselines/review?txt', matching both review.txt and review_txt exactly as the BRE did), also FAILS that test. One fixture, three arms, no regression.

(2) BOTH ROUND-6/7 MAJORS STAY CLOSED. Dropping ` -- baselines/review.txt` from the gate's `git diff --cached` fails anArgumentInADIFFERENTSTAGEDFileDoesNOTLiftTheCap (and aFILENAMEThatMerely...). Replacing the no-task guard with `if false` fails verdictsThatNameNOTASKRefuseRatherThanCountingAsROUNDZERO.

(3) NO TEST LOST FALSIFIABILITY, and this was established by measurement rather than by diffing against the previous round. A 19-mutation sweep over the changed production code shows every one of the 15 tests is killed by at least one mutation, with each test's stated purpose killed by the mutation it names: cap-at-1 -> withinTheCap; cap removed / ARGUED always 1 -> the ten 'does NOT lift' tests; ARGUED never set -> overTheCapWithASTAGEDArgument; task dropped from the key -> anArgumentForADIFFERENTTask + aTASKNameIsMatchedEXACTLY; worktree read instead of index -> anUNSTAGED, worktree-of-a-staged-file, ALREADY-COMMITTED, DIFF-CONTEXT, decoy-FILENAME; reason requirement dropped -> aROUNDSKeyWithNOREASON; `finish` inserted after the argued `warn` -> anARGUEDCapStillBLOCKSAnUnresolvedMajor; disagreement refusal disabled -> verdictsDISAGREEING.

(3a) THE CAP-REMOVED MUTATION IS THE ANTI-VACUITY PROBE AND IT PASSES CLEANLY: replacing `if [ "${ROUNDS:-0}" -gt 2 ]` with `if false` fails exactly the ten 'does NOT lift the cap' tests. So none of them is refusing for the wrong reason (a missing verdict, a fixture that never staged anything) -- each is refusing ON THE CAP, which is the failure mode this file's own comments record being caught on twice.

(3b) THE T7 COMMENT IS NOW ACCURATE, verified rather than accepted. Dropping the added-line guard so ANY diff line argues fails ONLY aROUNDSLineAppearingOnlyAsDIFFCONTEXT and NOT aROUNDSLineALREADYCOMMITTED -- exactly what the revised comment at line 356-366 claims. I could construct no mutation the HISTORY test kills and the context test does not, so 'a strict subset, kept for readability' is the correct description and no longer overclaims.

(4) THE RECORDED MINORS DID NOT GET WORSE, and one is better than recorded. T3 (exact field match -> substring, `index(f[1], k)`): still survives, 15/15 green, unchanged. T4 both arms: dropping the both-roles PRESENCE loop survives, and narrowing the unresolved-majors loop to the first role survives -- both unchanged. T5: the digits guard (`case "$ROUNDS" in ''|*[!0-9]*`) is still individually deletable with 15/15 green. BUT the stderr arm of T5 is NOT as recorded: mutating `2>"$ERRS"` back to `2>&1` -- the fail-open defect the comment at check-reviewed.sh:59-65 exists for -- IS KILLED, by verdictsDISAGREEINGAboutTheTaskAreREFUSEDRatherThanResolved. So the substantive half of that comment is pinned; only the `[ -n "$WHY" ] ||` fallback message and the digits guard are not.

(5) ONE EQUIVALENT MUTANT FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT FILED, on the same reasoning round 7 used for the `ls` conjunct. Deleting the comment-skip `if (line ~ /^[[:space:]]*#/) next` from the awk survives 15/15, but it is unreachable: awk's `split(line, f, /[[:space:]]+/)` gives f[1]="#rounds:M9.1" for `#rounds:M9.1  x`, f[1]="#" for `# rounds:M9.1 x`, and f[1]="" for any leading-whitespace form -- verified by running awk directly. No comment line can ever produce f[1] == "rounds:<task>", so no input distinguishes the mutant. Not a finding.

TIER AND STANDARDS: correct tier. This is harness logic whose subject IS a shell gate over a git index, so exec'ing bash and git is the behaviour under test, not I/O smuggled into business logic -- non-negotiable 7 is not engaged. No Thread.sleep, no fixed port, no mock. The suite is wired: check-harness-tests.sh selects on `scripts/*.sh` and `buildSrc/*`, both changed, and buildSrc/build.gradle.kts declares ../scripts/*.sh as a task input so a gate edit is not reported UP-TO-DATE.

NOT FILED, pre-existing: @TempDir resolves to the system temp directory, which testing.md rule 17 forbids in favour of build/tmp. 9 of the 16 harness suites already do this and buildSrc's test task sets no java.io.tmpdir, so it is an established repo-wide convention rather than a regression introduced here. It belongs in a standards row, not as a finding against M4.21.

All 15 tests carry a red record in .harness/tdd/red.json. Note for the author, not a finding: those records key on the fully-qualified method name only, so a fixture BODY change (this round's decoy strengthening) does not re-key -- the gate could not have demanded a fresh red run for it, which is why the falsifiability above was re-measured rather than taken from the gate.
